weapon: One-Handed Blunt Weapon or One-Handed Axe (the two are identical in damage; the choice is cosmetic only)
archetype: Melee STR warrior that spends a per-character resource pool called Demon Fury (abbreviated DF in community docs) instead of MP. Burst is built around the Demon Awakening window, during which Demon Lash becomes empowered and is spammed off a limited stack pool, with Demon Impact used when lash stacks or the ring window run out. Outside of Awakening the class cycles Demon Chain and the empowered version of Cerberus Chomp off cooldown. High survivability, naturally high IED, and an unusually low-effort farming pattern built on Chaos Lock teleporting. Community source describes it as a strong beginner class.
resourceNameNote: The resource is DEMON FURY, not 'Demon Force'. maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills never uses the string 'Demon Force' (it uses Fury throughout: Fury Unleashed, Max Fury, Focused Fury, Reduce Fury), maplestorywiki.net/w/Hyper_Stats names the hyper stat 'Demon Fury / Time Force' and describes it as increasing 'Max Demon Fury for Demon Slayer', and Grandis Library states plainly 'Demon Slayers do not use MP and instead use Fury for their skills.' The class FAQ is internally inconsistent - its heading reads 'What is Demon Force (DF)' while the very next line reads 'Demon Slayers start with a base of 10 Demon Fury (DF)'. This file uses Demon Fury and keeps the community abbreviation DF. Verified 2026-09-12.

linkSkill.name: Fury Unleashed
linkSkill.effect: Boss Damage on the linked character. The Demon Slayer's own version of the skill additionally grants Fury Absorption; only the Boss Damage portion is listed for the Link Skill form.
linkSkill.levels: Lv1 = Boss Damage +10%, Lv2 = +15%, Lv3 = +20%. Confirmed identically by maplestorywiki.net/w/Fury_Unleashed and by Grandis Library's Demon Slayer page.

legionEffect: Abnormal Status Resistance +1 / +2 / +3 / +4 / +5, scaling with legion rank.

priority.node: Skill node priority order: 1. Demon Awakening, 2. Demon Bane, 3. Orthrus, 4. Spirit of Rage, 5. Weapon Aura, 6. Otherworld Goddess's Blessing, 7. Defender of the Demon
priority.why: This is the ordering the class doc publishes for levelling V skill nodes. Demon Awakening heads the list because the burst window is built entirely around it, and Demon Bane is the second burst component used inside that window.
priority.nameCorrections: The class doc writes entry 6 as "Otherworld's Goddess' Blessing" and entry 7 as "Mastema". Neither string is a node name in game. maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills lists the Shared V Skill as OTHERWORLD GODDESS'S BLESSING, and it lists no skill called Mastema at all: Mastema is the ally summoned by the V skill DEFENDER OF THE DEMON ("Summons loyal Mastema to fight by your side", Master Level 30), who casts Mastema's Claw and Mastema's Mark. The class doc uses 'Mastema' as shorthand for that skill throughout, including in its burst sequence. Both names corrected here so a player searching their V matrix finds the node. Verified against the wiki on 2026-09-12.
priority.consensusReason: The ORDER is stated by one source lane only (the Demon Slayer Discord FAQ). No independent source publishes a competing or confirming V skill node order. maplestorywiki is cited for the node NAMES only and casts no vote on the ordering.

priority.node: Boost node trio 1: Demon Lash + Demon Impact + Cerberus Chomp
priority.why: Groups the two skills that carry the burst and the off-burst rotation (Demon Lash during Awakening, Demon Impact outside it) with Cerberus Chomp, whose empowered version is used off cooldown after Awakening ends.
priority.consensusReason: The identical trio is published by two independent authors: the Demon Slayer Discord FAQ (2026-07-01) and mastermysty's cross-class node reference (page 2024-11-21, data 2024-05-14, where it is listed as 'Trio #1'). Grandis Library also publishes it, labelled 'Primary Trio', but credits the Demon Slayer Discord and links the class FAQ in its own further-reading block, so it restates lane 1 and is not a third vote.

priority.node: Boost node trio 2: Infernal Concussion + Demon Cry + Dark Metamorphosis
priority.why: Covers the mobbing skill plus the two skills whose uptime the class depends on: Demon Cry applies the boss debuff that keeps the Insult to Injury passive active, and Dark Metamorphosis is a major damage buff.
priority.orderingNote: The three members are an unordered set. The FAQ lists them Infernal Concussion / Demon Cry / Dark Metamorphosis, mastermysty lists them Demon Cry / Infernal Concussion / Dark Metamorphosis, and Grandis lists them Infernal Concussion / Demon Cry / Dark Metamorphosis. No source ranks within the trio, and Grandis's own note says 'any combination of these skills are good'.
priority.consensusReason: Same two independent authors publish the identical set (mastermysty as 'Trio #2'). Grandis labels it 'Secondary Trio' but is the same lane as the FAQ.

priority.node: Native boost node groupings (which skills share a node), as catalogued by Grandis Library: Node 1 = Demon Impact + Grim Scythe; Node 2 = Demon Lash + Infernal Concussion + Vortex of Doom; Node 3 = Dark Metamorphosis + Demon Cry; Node 4 = Cerberus Chomp + Binding Darkness; Node 5 = Judgment + Raven Storm + Carrion Breath; Node 6 = Chaos Lock + Dark Thrust + Soul Eater. TIERING: Grandis marks Nodes 1, 2, 3 and 4 as PRIMARY and Nodes 5 and 6 as OTHER. It assigns NO node to the SECONDARY tier for this class.
priority.why: Grandis Library's legend defines PRIMARY as 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used', SECONDARY as nodes that do not unlock a HEXA Mastery but are still used, and OTHER as nodes that 'do not need to be upgraded or has least priority'. So for Demon Slayer the four nodes worth upgrading are 1-4, and nodes 5-6 are the ones to leave alone.
priority.correction: An earlier revision of this file recorded Node 4 and Node 5 as SECONDARY and only Nodes 1-3 as PRIMARY. That is wrong. The page's own data object gives primary = nodes [1,2,3,4] and other = nodes [5,6], with no secondary list at all. Re-read and corrected 2026-09-12.
priority.orderingNote: Node numbering is Grandis's catalogue index, not a levelling order. Nodes 1-4 are a flat PRIMARY tier with no rank between them.
priority.consensusReason: Single source, and that source credits the Demon Slayer Discord for its boost node build, so it is the same lane as the class FAQ rather than an independent confirmation. All six groupings and both tier assignments were read directly off the page on 2026-09-12.

trios.trio: Demon Lash, Demon Impact, Cerberus Chomp
trios.role: Build first. mastermysty calls it 'Trio #1'; Grandis Library calls it the 'Primary Trio'. Neither source splits Demon Slayer's trios by bossing versus mobbing.
trios.consensusReason: Two independent sources (FAQ lane, mastermysty). Grandis agrees but is the FAQ lane restated.

trios.trio: Infernal Concussion, Demon Cry, Dark Metamorphosis
trios.role: Build second. mastermysty calls it 'Trio #2'; Grandis Library calls it the 'Secondary Trio'. Neither source splits Demon Slayer's trios by bossing versus mobbing.
trios.orderingNote: Members unordered; the three sources list them in two different internal orders.
trios.consensusReason: Two independent sources (FAQ lane, mastermysty). Grandis agrees but is the FAQ lane restated.

vMatrix.notes: Two different things are recorded above and should not be confused. The 'trios' are the crafted boost node combinations the community recommends building; the relative order BETWEEN the two trios is stated by both independent sources (trio 1 before trio 2), while the order WITHIN each trio is not. The 'native boost node groupings' are the fixed families the game itself uses to decide which skills a given boost node can boost; that list comes from Grandis Library and is useful for knowing which node unlocks which HEXA Mastery, not for choosing what to craft. Grandis adds two mechanical notes worth keeping: four boost nodes in total are needed to reach Master Level 60 on these skills once matrix points are used, and two nodes with the same main skill (the skill at the top of the node) cannot be equipped at the same time. Grandis is stamped GMS Ver. 269 and also exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which is direct evidence that node groupings changed at v269; the mastermysty reference predates that (data stated as 2024-05-14, page last updated 2024-11-21, both strings read off the page) yet still lists the same two trios, which is why the trios are rated moderate rather than weak. No source found gives an explicit boost-node-vs-skill-node levelling sequence for Demon Slayer.

order.step: 1. Unlock the five highest-value nodes first, in this order: mastery core labelled M4, HEXA Demon Lash, mastery core labelled M3, HEXA Demon Impact, Sol Hecate.
order.why: These are the five largest single-level final damage gains in the class doc's model, by a wide margin: the first level of each is worth 9.9, 8.8, 6.5, 3.7 and 4.84 final damage respectively, against roughly 0.2-0.4 for almost every level that follows. Re-read off the sheet's CSV export on 2026-09-12; the first five data rows are M4 0-1 = 9.9, Lash 0-1 = 8.8, M3 0-1 = 6.5, Impact 0-1 = 3.7, Hecate 0-1 = 4.84, exactly as stated. (An earlier revision of this file said 'the four highest-value nodes' and then listed five; corrected.)
order.consensusReason: Single source lane. The ordering comes from one spreadsheet published by the Demon Slayer Discord FAQ; the sheet is the FAQ's own linked model, not a second opinion. No independent source publishes a Demon Slayer HEXA order - Grandis Library has no HEXA section for this class at all.

order.step: 2. Unlock the enhancement cores in this order as they become affordable: Demon Awakening (around step 7 of the model), Demon Bane (step 12), Orthrus (step 22), the core the sheet labels 'Snake' (step 35), then Amethystine Incursion, the Ascent skill (step 44).
order.why: Same model. Each unlock is worth well under 2 final damage but still outranks most individual level-ups at the point it appears.
order.consensusReason: Single source lane (FAQ plus its own linked spreadsheet).

order.step: 3. Push to the level 10 breakpoints in this order: HEXA Demon Impact, Demon Awakening, HEXA Demon Lash, M4, Demon Bane, M3, Orthrus, Nightmare (Origin), Sol Hecate, 'Snake', Amethystine Incursion.
order.why: HEXA nodes have cost/benefit breakpoints at levels 10, 20 and 30, and the model's step ordering sequences those crossings this way.
order.consensusReason: Single source lane (the FAQ's own spreadsheet).

order.step: 4. Push to the level 20 breakpoints in this order: HEXA Demon Impact, HEXA Demon Lash, Demon Awakening, M4, Demon Bane, M3, Nightmare (Origin), Sol Hecate, Orthrus, 'Snake', Amethystine Incursion.
order.consensusReason: Single source lane (the FAQ's own spreadsheet).

order.step: 5. Take nodes to level 30 in this order: HEXA Demon Impact, Demon Awakening, Nightmare (Origin), HEXA Demon Lash, Sol Hecate, M4, Demon Bane, Orthrus, M3, 'Snake', Amethystine Incursion last.
order.why: Same model. Amethystine Incursion (Ascent) is the last node maxed in this ordering, and the class doc notes that if your boss runs are faster than the 30 minute reference fight, Ascent's value rises sharply - which would pull it forward.
order.consensusReason: Single source lane; the source itself flags the ordering as sensitive to fight length.

order.step: HEXA Stat: newer characters should put points into all HEXA Stat nodes once the first Demon Awakening step is done. For more progressed characters the class doc declines to give a fixed rule and tells the reader to compare against the final damage figures in the spreadsheet instead.
order.why: Stated directly by the class doc: 'Newer players should invest in all hexastats upon finishing Awakening 1. For more progressed characters its less clear but you can estimate it based off of the FD gains from the sheet.'

order.step: Sol Hecate binding: bind Sol Hecate: Styx to the Angelic Buster link skill, and keep a separate keybind for Styx so it can be cast manually when the AB link cooldown is skipped or when it needs recasting mid-burst. Bind Sol Hecate: Phlegethon to an early skill in the burst sequence such as Demon Awakening; Demon Bane also works and is the better choice on a 17-burst run.
order.why: Stated directly by the class doc. Skill names Sol Hecate: Styx and Sol Hecate: Phlegethon confirmed on maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills under Shared HEXA Skills (the four Sol Hecate branches are Styx, Charon, Phlegethon and Pactum).
order.consensusReason: Single source lane for the judgement; the wiki confirms names only.

order.step: HEXA reset for Sol Hecate: a small gain at best. The class doc's own observation is that the best way to free up resources is to drop M3 and M4 to 29, sacrifice however many Ascent levels you are willing to give up, and only then drain Spirit of Rage - and this only applies if those nodes were already maxed.
order.why: Demon Slayer has no genuinely weak HEXA skills to strip, so a reset recovers little. The class doc's wording is 'because Demon Slayer has no "bad skills" it will be a fairly low gain'.
order.consensusReason: Single source lane, and the source presents it as a personal observation ('My observation is...') rather than a tested result.

hexa.notes: IMPORTANT LIMITATION ON THE ORDER ABOVE. The spreadsheet the class doc publishes uses shorthand labels and does not expand all of them. 'Lash' and 'Impact' map cleanly to the HEXA Demon Lash and HEXA Demon Impact mastery cores, 'Hecate' to Sol Hecate, 'Nightmare' to the Origin skill and 'Ascent' to Amethystine Incursion (both confirmed on maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills, which files Nightmare and Amethystine Incursion under Class-Specific HEXA Skills). 'M3' and 'M4' are structurally the third and fourth HEXA Mastery cores, but the source never says which skills they are, and they are NOT resolved here. WHAT THE WIKI ACTUALLY LISTS (re-read section by section on 2026-09-12): the Mastery Skills section holds EIGHT entries - HEXA Demon Impact, HEXA Demon Impact: Demon Chain, HEXA Demon Lash, HEXA Infernal Concussion, HEXA Demon Cry, HEXA Dark Metamorphosis, HEXA Cerberus Chomp and Demonic Plume. The Class-Specific HEXA Skills section holds only TWO - Nightmare and Amethystine Incursion. An earlier revision of this file listed seven mastery skills (omitting Demonic Plume) and wrongly placed Demonic Plume among the class-specific HEXA skills; both errors are corrected here. The consequence is that M3 and M4 are two of SIX mastery candidates, not two of four: HEXA Demon Impact: Demon Chain, HEXA Infernal Concussion, HEXA Demon Cry, HEXA Dark Metamorphosis, HEXA Cerberus Chomp, Demonic Plume. Do not guess between them. 'Snake' is likewise unexpanded; the wiki lists exactly four HEXA Enhancement cores for Demon Slayer (Demon Awakening Boost, Spirit of Rage Boost, Orthrus Boost, Demon Bane Boost - all four re-read on 2026-09-12), the spreadsheet separately tracks Awakening, Bane and Orthrus, and the FAQ's reset advice names 'Spirit of Rage' in prose exactly where the sheet writes 'Snake', so by elimination 'Snake' is the Spirit of Rage enhancement core. That is an inference from node count plus the prose match, not something any source states outright. MODEL ASSUMPTIONS: the class doc states the ordering is derived from a 16-burst, 30-minute boss fight and that faster runs raise Ascent's value substantially. Grandis Library's Demon Slayer page has no HEXA section at all, so there is no second published Demon Slayer HEXA ordering to compare against. The class doc also publishes the same path as an infographic (hexa_path.png); it is an image and has not been read, so nothing in this file depends on it.

hyperStats.orderingNote: THIS IS AN UNORDERED SET, NOT A PRIORITY RANKING. No source publishes a Demon Slayer hyper stat priority order. Array position below carries no meaning and must not be read as rank. Both entries are recorded with rank null for that reason.

priority.stat: Demon Fury (the hyper stat maplestorywiki names 'Demon Fury / Time Force', which increases Max Demon Fury for Demon Slayer and Time Force for Zero)
priority.detail: Around 5 points is the figure the class doc gives: 'You can also add points in Hyper Stats for DF (usually 5 points is recommended).' Demon Slayer starts from a base of 10 DF and the rest of the pool comes from the secondary weapon, so hyper stat points are a supplementary source rather than the main one.
priority.nameCorrection: An earlier revision of this file called this stat 'Demon Force'. The hyper stat is Demon Fury; corrected against maplestorywiki.net/w/Hyper_Stats on 2026-09-12.
priority.consensusReason: Single source lane for the 5-point figure; the wiki confirms the stat's name only.

priority.detail: Hyper stats are named as one of the sources a Demon Slayer must combine with links and legion to reach 100% critical rate naturally. The class doc's wording is 'You will need to hit 100% crit through some combination of links, legion, hyper stats, etc.' It does not say how many points to spend, only that the 100% target must be met.
priority.consensusReason: Single source lane for the hyper stat framing; the underlying reason (Dark Metamorphosis, Cerberus Chomp and Demonic Plume do not auto-crit) is stated by the same source.

hyperStats.notes: NO COMPLETE HYPER STAT ORDERING WAS FOUND FOR DEMON SLAYER IN ANY SOURCE. The class doc gives only the two entries above and ranks neither against the other. Grandis Library's Demon Slayer page carries no hyper stat section at all (re-checked 2026-09-12 against the page's own data object, whose keys are classGroup, jobGroup, mainStat, secondaryStat, legion, legionValue, equipment, innerAbility, attackStats, buffInfo, linkSkill, buildPath, hyperBuild, nodeInfo, moreInfo, infographics, discord, credits, extraContent - there is no hyperStats key). mastermysty's reference is boost nodes only. This field is deliberately incomplete rather than filled in from a generic cross-class list, and it is deliberately flagged unordered rather than shipped as a ranked array. Note also that hyper stat allocation is a per-character calculation in current community practice rather than a fixed list, which is part of why no Demon Slayer source publishes one.

hyperSkills.orderingNote: The passives below are a SELECTION SET, not a priority order. The two sources list them in different sequences - the class doc gives Demon Impact, Dark Metamorphosis, Demon Lash; Grandis Library gives Demon Lash, Dark Metamorphosis, Demon Impact - so array position carries no meaning.

passives.skill: Demon Impact - Reinforce, Extra Strike, and Reduce Fury
passives.consensusReason: Two pages agree verbatim but Grandis Library's credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Demon Slayer Discord', the same Discord the class FAQ is compiled from, so this is one source lane agreeing with itself.

hyperSkills.activesNote: No source found recommends a hyper skill ACTIVE loadout for Demon Slayer, so that field is null rather than guessed. Cerberus Chomp is a hyper skill active - Grandis Library's own boost node alt text reads 'Cerberus Chomp (Hyper Skill)' - and the class doc's bossing rotation uses its empowered form off cooldown after Demon Awakening ends, so it is clearly taken in practice. Demonic Fortitude and Boundless Rage also appear as castables in the class doc's burst sequence and are hyper-skill-tier actives, but neither source presents an explicit active-skill selection list, so no active loadout is asserted here.
hyperSkills.notes: The three passives above are exactly the list both pages publish, re-read on 2026-09-12: the class doc's skills.md gives 'Demon Impact: Reinforce, Extra Strike, Reduce Fury / Dark Metamorphosis: Reinforce / Demon Lash: Reinforce', and Grandis Library's Hyper Skill Passive Build block gives the same three in the reverse order. Note that the passive selection matches the crafted boost node trios, since Demon Impact, Demon Lash and Dark Metamorphosis are all in them.

bossing.consensusReason: Both pages trace to the Demon Slayer Discord, so one lane. The class doc lists it as mandatory line 1; Grandis lists it first under 'For Bossing'.

bossing.line: Damage to monsters inflicted with an Abnormal Status +8%
bossing.why: Demon Slayer keeps a debuff on the boss at essentially all times (Demon Cry and Demon Chain apply it), so this line is close to permanently live.
bossing.consensusReason: Both pages trace to the Demon Slayer Discord, so one lane. Both list it second.

bossing.line: Third line is CONTESTED - see the conflicts array. The class doc gives Attack +21 or Buff Duration +38%, chosen by legion progression; Grandis Library gives Chance to Skip Cooldown +10% or Buff Duration +38%. Both agree Buff Duration +38% is a valid choice; they differ on the alternative.
bossing.why: The class doc's stated rule is that Buff Duration is the better line at lower legion, where roughly 110% buff duration cannot otherwise be reached, and that Attack +21 overtakes it once legion is high enough. It names the SHINE link skill as what makes high buff duration reachable without spending the inner ability line on it.
bossing.consensusReason: Contested within a single source lane - both restatements come from the same Discord, so one of them is most likely stale. Not resolved here.

training.line: Meso Obtained or Item Drop Rate +20%
training.consensusReason: Single source (Grandis Library, which credits the Demon Slayer Discord). The class doc publishes no training inner ability set.

training.line: Meso Obtained or Item Drop Rate +15%
training.detail: Grandis attaches a note to this set: 'Depending on what's chosen as the 1st Line, choose the other for the 2nd Line' - i.e. take Meso Obtained on one line and Item Drop Rate on the other, not the same stat twice.

avoid.why: Demon Slayer already reaches Attack Speed +8 (AS2) natively with a Fast weapon, so the attack speed inner ability line is wasted. The class doc says outright 'You do NOT need the +1 Inner Ability.' The remaining gap to the Attack Speed +10 cap is covered by a Monster Park green potion plus Decent Speed Infusion.
avoid.consensusReason: Single source lane, but stated explicitly and unambiguously. Grandis independently lists the class's base Attack Speed as 8, which corroborates the premise but not the recommendation.

avoid.line: Chance to Skip Cooldown - situationally harmful while TP farming
avoid.why: The class doc's farming section lists cooldown skip first among the causes of running out of Demon Fury: 'If your Inner Ability or Artifacts have Cooldown Skip, you will sometimes chaos lock twice in a row. This consumes extra DF, so you should spec out of CD skip if you are having issues.' This does not apply to bossing, where the class doc treats cooldown reduction as valuable - and note Grandis lists Chance to Skip Cooldown +10% as a bossing line.

innerAbility.notes: Both published inner ability lists come from the same origin (the Demon Slayer Discord) - Grandis Library's credits block names it explicitly and Grandis also links the class FAQ in its own further-reading block - so the apparent agreement between the two pages is one source restating itself, not two votes. Every line above was re-read off the live pages on 2026-09-12: the class doc's gear.md publishes the bossing set as numbered 'Mandatory lines' 1/2/3, and Grandis's page data carries the bossing and training sets verbatim as recorded. The third bossing line is the one place the two restatements diverge; that divergence is recorded in the conflicts array rather than resolved.

gearingNotes:
DEMON FURY CHANGES SECONDARY WEAPON SELECTION. Demon Slayer spends Demon Fury (DF) rather than MP. The base pool is 10 and almost all of it comes from the Demon Aegis secondary: Force Shield of Extremes gives +110 DF, Princess No's Accursed Shield +173 DF, and Ruin Force Shield +100 DF. Ruin Force Shield is stated as best in slot despite having the smallest DF pool, because it grants 10% final damage at the cost of taking 15% more damage; it drops from Damien and can be pitied with Dawn Whisper Cores. Princess No's Accursed Shield is named as a good early-game option for its DF and stats. Around 5 hyper stat points into Demon Fury supplement the pool. (Terminology note: the class doc heads this section 'What is Demon Force (DF)' but its own first sentence says 'Demon Fury'; the game term is Demon Fury. See resourceNameNote.)

CRITICAL RATE MUST REACH 100% FROM GEAR, LINKS, LEGION AND HYPER STATS. Dark Metamorphosis, Cerberus Chomp and Demonic Plume do not auto-crit, so Demon Slayer cannot lean on the usual assumption that crit rate above the class's passive floor is wasted. This is the single biggest class-specific gearing difference and it changes link, legion and hyper stat allocation.

ATTACK SPEED. AS +8 (AS2) is reached natively with a Fast weapon, so the +1 attack speed inner ability line is not needed. A Monster Park green potion plus Decent Speed Infusion takes the character to the AS +10 cap, which the class doc values at roughly 6% final damage.

WEAPON CHOICE IS COSMETIC. One-handed axe and one-handed blunt weapon are equivalent in damage.

WSE POTENTIALS. Target zero IED lines long term; either nine attack lines, or eight attack lines plus one boss line. The class doc expects nine attack lines to become strictly optimal once the Astra secondary arrives.

COOLDOWN HAT IS USED. Cooldown reduction holds solid value down to -4, after which it becomes diminishing on Cerberus Chomp and Demon Chain. The class doc's testing places -4 at roughly 3 final damage and -2 at roughly 1 final damage, and publishes this Reboot endgame hat ranking: (1) -4 plus a stat line, (2) 39 STR, (3) -2 plus 26 STR, (4) 36 STR, (5) -2 plus 23 STR or plain -4, (6) 33 STR, (7) -2 plus 20 STR, (8) -3 plus any stat line. A cooldown hat also prevents a party-play desync risk when the buff sequence is used after the Origin skill.

IED. The class doc describes Demon Slayer's IED as naturally high, which is consistent with the advice to avoid IED lines on WSE.

LINK SKILLS. The class doc gives a drop order for when links must be cut: Ark, then Demon Avenger, then Xenon, then Thief. It names Luminous and Lynn links as good flex options for characters with a less developed legion, and says survival links can be flexed out if needed. The full recommended link set is published only as an image and has not been transcribed here.

commonMistakes.detail: Demon Cry and Demon Chain apply a debuff that lowers the boss's PDR and accuracy. The accuracy component is what triggers the Insult to Injury passive, worth 15% final damage, so the debuff needs to be up continuously. In the culvert rotation the class doc even uses Erda bind on the first stage that does not instantly die, purely so the debuff can be applied during Demon Bane.
The class doc recommends putting Dark Metamorphosis on auto-buff specifically because forgetting to refresh it is a severe damage loss.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling +1 attack speed on inner ability
commonMistakes.detail: Unnecessary; the class already reaches AS2 with a Fast weapon.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming crit rate above the class passive floor is wasted
commonMistakes.detail: Three Demon Slayer skills do not auto-crit, so the 100% natural crit rate target is real for this class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Carrying cooldown skip into TP farming
commonMistakes.detail: Cooldown skip can cause a double Chaos Lock, which consumes extra Demon Fury and is one of the named causes of running out of DF while farming.

commonMistakes.mistake: Still farming with Infernal Concussion after v269
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc says HEXA Infernal Concussion became awkward to turn off as of v269 and now recommends TP farming with Demon Lash instead. It flags the tradeoffs: Demon Lash farming may not full clear without Sol Janus at 30, will fail to full clear during boosters (swap back to Infernal Concussion then), and carries a higher damage requirement.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using regular Cerberus Chomp after Demon Awakening ends
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc specifies the empowered version, not the regular one, in the post-Awakening loop alongside Demon Chain.

commonMistakes.mistake: Searching the V matrix for 'Mastema' or 'Otherworld's Goddess' Blessing'
commonMistakes.detail: Neither string is a node name. The class doc's shorthand 'Mastema' means the V skill DEFENDER OF THE DEMON, which summons the ally Mastema; and the node is spelled OTHERWORLD GODDESS'S BLESSING. Both confirmed on maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills.

sources.what: Demon Slayer FAQ, self-described as compiled from the Demon Slayer Discord. The primary judgement source for this class and the origin of nearly every priority claim in this file: Demon Fury mechanics and secondary weapon DF values, the 100% crit rate requirement and why, attack speed, hyper skill passives, V matrix skill node priority and both boost node trios, HEXA investment order (via its linked spreadsheet and an infographic), Sol Hecate binding, HEXA reset guidance, inner ability lines, WSE potential targets, cooldown hat ranking, bossing and culvert rotations, and TP farming. Note it is a JavaScript-rendered page; the readable content lives as markdown in the GitHub repository at https://github.com/mafhcow/demon-slayer-faq under content/ (basics.md, bossing.md, farming.md, gear.md, skills.md - all five re-fetched raw on 2026-09-12).

The HEXA investment model the class doc links. An ordered list of (node, from level, to level, final damage gained) with 156 data rows, derived from a 16-burst 30-minute boss fight. This is where the entire HEXA order in this file comes from. Uses unexpanded shorthand labels M3, M4 and Snake. Exportable as CSV at .../export?format=csv - re-exported and spot-checked 2026-09-12.

sources.what: Grandis Library Demon Slayer page. Source for the native boost node groupings with PRIMARY/OTHER tiering (nodes 1-4 primary, nodes 5-6 other, no secondary tier assigned for this class), the recommended trios labelled Primary Trio and Secondary Trio, the hyper skill passive build, recommended inner ability split bossing vs training, base stats, weapon multiplier (1.2x), and the class's V skill list. Has NO HEXA section and NO hyper stat section. Its credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Demon Slayer Discord', and its further-reading block links the class FAQ directly, which is why it is marked not independent - it restates the same Discord the class FAQ comes from. Machine-readable: the page ships its full data object in a __NEXT_DATA__ script tag, which is how the node tiering was read.

conflicts.topic: Third inner ability line for bossing
conflicts.positionA: Attack +21, or Buff Duration +38% at lower legion. The class doc's rule is that buff duration wins while roughly 110% buff duration is otherwise unreachable, and that Attack +21 overtakes it once legion is developed enough (it names the SHINE link skill as what makes high buff duration reachable without the inner ability line).
conflicts.positionB: Chance to Skip Cooldown +10%, or Buff Duration +38%.
conflicts.note: NOT an independent disagreement. Both pages credit the Demon Slayer Discord, so this is one source lane contradicting itself - most likely one of the two restatements is stale. Both options are recorded rather than picked. The two agree on Buff Duration +38% as one valid choice; they differ on the alternative (Attack +21 versus Chance to Skip Cooldown +10%). Note separately that the class doc's farming section advises speccing OUT of cooldown skip when Demon Fury runs dry while TP farming, which is an argument against the Grandis line for a character that also farms. Both positions re-read off the live pages 2026-09-12.

conflicts.positionA: The two trios are current as of the 2026-07-01 class doc revision.
conflicts.positionB: The same two trios were already published in 2024, from data the author dates to 2024-05-14.
conflicts.note: Not a contradiction - they agree, and Grandis Library agrees too (as Primary Trio / Secondary Trio). Recorded because Grandis exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which shows that node groupings did change at v269 for at least some classes. The fact that the 2024 trios still match the 2026 class doc is evidence Demon Slayer's trios were not disturbed, but it has not been positively confirmed against a v.271 source.

evidenceNotes: FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCE LANES WERE REACHED, BUT ONLY TWO CARRY JUDGEMENT. The lanes are (1) the Demon Slayer Discord's FAQ, (2) mastermysty's node reference, (3) maplestorywiki.net, and (4) Grandis Library - but lane 4 is NOT independent: it credits the Demon Slayer Discord for its inner ability, hyper passive and boost node builds, and links the class FAQ in its own further-reading block, so it collapses into lane 1. Lane 3 carries facts only - skill names, hyper stat names, link skill values, legion effect - and no priorities at all. Lane 2 covers boost node trios and nothing else. That means EVERY HEXA, hyper stat, hyper skill and inner ability claim in this file rests on a single source lane, and every one of them is labelled sourceCount 1 / consensus weak accordingly. The only claims at sourceCount 2 / moderate are the two boost node trios. NOTHING in this file is labelled strong, and nothing should be until a genuine third judgement lane is found. Still not performed: Reddit could not be reached from the research environment, and NamuWiki's Demon Slayer page (linked by Grandis) is JavaScript-rendered and returned no readable content, so the KMS-side cross-check that might form a third judgement lane is still missing. A follow-up pass should target: a 2025-2026 r/Maplestory Demon Slayer thread, the Demon Slayer Discord's own pinned infographics (including hexa_path.png and the 6th-job infographic Grandis credits to the Demon Slayer Discord, dated 2026-05-27), and a v.271-dated confirmation of the boost node trios. The class doc is stamped v269 and the target is v.271, so anything touching v270 or v271 balance changes is unverified and is labelled as a v269 claim rather than a current one.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionScope: Resolution pass covered the five endgame sections only: vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility. Defects concerning jobs 1-4 skill builds, skill damage coefficients, damage lines, job tiers and rotations were out of scope by product owner instruction and that content was left untouched.

resolved.defect: 'MASTEMA' IS NOT A NODE OR SKILL NAME - listed as V skill node priority #7.
resolved.what: Opened maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills with a browser user agent and parsed it by section. There is no skill named Mastema. Mastema is the ally summoned by the Shared V Skill DEFENDER OF THE DEMON ('Summons loyal Mastema to fight by your side', Master Level 30), who casts Mastema's Claw and Mastema's Mark. The class FAQ uses 'Mastema' as shorthand for that skill in both its V matrix priority list and its burst sequence. V skill node priority entry 7 is now 'Defender of the Demon', with the FAQ's shorthand recorded in a nameCorrections field so the mapping is traceable, and a commonMistakes entry added so a player who reads the FAQ knows what to search for. Claim kept, not deleted: the underlying node is real and the FAQ does rank it seventh.

resolved.defect: 'OTHERWORLD'S GODDESS' BLESSING' (V node priority #6) does not exist as written; the wiki name is OTHERWORLD GODDESS'S BLESSING.
resolved.what: Confirmed on maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills, which renders the Shared V Skill as 'Otherworld Goddess's Blessing' in both link text and file name, and independently on Grandis Library, whose icon alt text reads 'Otherworld Goddess's Blessing (5th Job)'. Spelling corrected in the priority list and recorded in commonMistakes.

resolved.defect: THE RESOURCE IS CALLED FURY, NOT 'DEMON FORCE'.
resolved.section: hyperStats (in scope) plus archetype and gearingNotes (outside the five endgame sections)
resolved.what: Confirmed the defect three ways: maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills never uses the string 'Demon Force'; maplestorywiki.net/w/Hyper_Stats names the stat 'Demon Fury / Time Force' and describes it as increasing 'Max Demon Fury for Demon Slayer'; Grandis Library says 'Demon Slayers do not use MP and instead use Fury for their skills.' The in-scope fix is hyperStats.priority[0], whose stat name was 'Demon Force' and is now 'Demon Fury' with the wiki cited. The terminology was also corrected in archetype, gearingNotes, innerAbility.avoid and commonMistakes - a rename only, no content added or removed there - and a resourceNameNote field records the evidence and the class doc's own internal inconsistency ('What is Demon Force (DF)' heading over a 'Demon Slayers start with a base of 10 Demon Fury (DF)' first line).

resolved.defect: THE MASTERY-SKILL LIST IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which breaks the M3/M4 reasoning.
resolved.what: Re-parsed the wiki page by section id. Mastery Skills holds EIGHT entries - HEXA Demon Impact, HEXA Demon Impact: Demon Chain, HEXA Demon Lash, HEXA Infernal Concussion, HEXA Demon Cry, HEXA Dark Metamorphosis, HEXA Cerberus Chomp and Demonic Plume. Class-Specific HEXA Skills holds exactly TWO - Nightmare and Amethystine Incursion. Both errors in the old hexa.notes (omitting Demonic Plume from mastery, and listing it as class-specific) are fixed, and the consequence is now stated correctly: M3 and M4 are two of SIX mastery candidates, not two of four. They remain deliberately unresolved rather than guessed. Also re-confirmed that the wiki lists exactly four HEXA Enhancement cores (Demon Awakening Boost, Spirit of Rage Boost, Orthrus Boost, Demon Bane Boost), so the 'Snake = Spirit of Rage' elimination still holds and stays flagged as an inference.

resolved.defect: EVERY OTHER NAME CHECKS OUT against maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Slayer/Skills (Grim Scythe, Vortex of Doom, Binding Darkness, Judgment, Raven Storm, Carrion Breath, Chaos Lock, Dark Thrust, Soul Eater, Insult to Injury, Demonic Plume, Weapon Aura, Nightmare, Amethystine Incursion, Sol Janus, Sol Hecate branches, Demon Awakening, Spirit of Rage, Orthrus, Demon Bane; Cerberus Chomp a Hyper Skill; Fury Unleashed 10/15/20%; legion effect verbatim; 'Snake = Spirit of Rage' correctly flagged as inference).
resolved.what: This entry was filed in the defects array but is a confirmation, not a defect. Independently re-verified on 2026-09-12 by re-fetching the wiki page and Grandis Library and re-reading them by section. No change required; every name listed is real and used correctly in this file.

resolved.defect: FOUND DURING THIS PASS, not in the contest report: the native boost node tiering was misattributed to Grandis Library. The file said Nodes 1-3 were PRIMARY, Nodes 4-5 SECONDARY and Node 6 OTHER.
resolved.what: Read Grandis Library's own page data object (shipped in its __NEXT_DATA__ script tag). Its nodeInfo gives primary = [0,1,2,3] and other = [4,5], with no secondary list for this class at all. So Node 4 (Cerberus Chomp + Binding Darkness) is PRIMARY, not SECONDARY, and Node 5 (Judgment + Raven Storm + Carrion Breath) is OTHER, not SECONDARY. This is a citation inversion of the same kind the contest pass was hunting: the file was relegating a node the cited source promotes. Corrected, with the legend definitions quoted and the prior error recorded inline. The six group memberships themselves were re-read from the page's alt text and were already exact.

resolved.defect: FOUND DURING THIS PASS: hyperStats.priority shipped as an ordered array while no source ranks Demon Slayer hyper stats, and hyperSkills.passives shipped as an ordered array while the two cited pages list the three passives in opposite orders.
resolved.what: hyperStats now carries ordered:false with an explicit orderingNote, and each entry carries rank:null, so downstream code cannot read array position as priority. Re-confirmed that Grandis Library has no hyper stat section at all by listing the keys of its page data object. hyperSkills now carries ordered:false because the class doc lists Demon Impact / Dark Metamorphosis / Demon Lash while Grandis lists Demon Lash / Dark Metamorphosis / Demon Impact - the set is agreed, the sequence is not. Boost node trio 2 and the Grandis node tiering were flagged unordered for the same reason. vMatrix skill node priority, the hexa steps and the inner ability lines keep ordered:true because their sources state those orders explicitly (numbered lists in the FAQ, step sequence in the spreadsheet).

clearedOnInspection: NO FABRICATED PRIORITY ORDERS. The contest agent exported the HEXA spreadsheet (docs.google.com/.../export?format=csv) and machine-checked every ordering claim: 156 data rows as stated; step 1 unlock order M4/Lash/M3/Impact/Hecate with FD 9.9/8.8/6.5/3.7/4.84; step 2 unlock step numbers Awakening=7, Bane=12, Orthrus=22, Snake=35, Ascent=44; level-10 crossing order Impact, Awakening, Lash, M4, Bane, M3, Orthrus, Nightmare, Hecate, Snake, Ascent; level-20 order Impact, Lash, Awakening, M4, Bane, M3, Nightmare, Hecate, Orthrus, Snake, Ascent; level-30 order Impact, Awakening, Nightmare, Lash, Hecate, M4, Bane, Orthrus, M3, Snake, Ascent. Every one matches the file character for character. It also pulled the FAQ's raw markdown from github.com/mafhcow/demon-slayer-faq/content/{basics,bossing,farming,gear,skills}.md and found the V skill node list, both trios, the three hyper passives, the three IA lines, the eight-entry cooldown hat ranking, the three shield DF values (110/173/100) and the link drop order (Ark, DA, Xenon, Thief) all faithful and properly paraphrased. Not re-litigated in this pass; the CSV export was re-fetched on 2026-09-12 only to confirm the sheet is still live and that its first five rows still read M4 9.9, Lash 8.8, M3 6.5, Impact 3.7, Hecate 4.84.
contest.shipReadyNote: The five endgame sections now contain no claim pointing at a source that does not support it, and no node or skill name that could not be found in a reachable source. Two items remain open but are labelled gaps rather than unverified claims: the identity of the spreadsheet's M3 and M4 mastery cores (six candidates, deliberately not guessed) and the third bossing inner ability line (contested within one source lane, both options recorded). Every endgame claim carries sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt, and none is labelled stronger than the evidence supports - the maximum anywhere in this file is moderate at sourceCount 2, on the two boost node trios.
